test_cases.title: Raw IMU Record Write - Round Trip
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog library against a tmpfs/in-memory storage backend with a fresh run.
procedure: Construct a raw IMU sample record with known accelerometer and gyroscope values.
Call the mlog write API for IMU records with the constructed sample.
Close or flush the run to ensure bytes are durable.
Re-open the produced log file and parse records using the documented format.
Locate the IMU record and compare every field against the input sample.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Write API returns success and the parsed IMU record exactly matches the input accelerometer and gyroscope values, with the record type identifying it as an IMU record.

test_cases.title: Raw Barometer Record Write - Round Trip
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog library against a tmpfs/in-memory storage backend with a fresh run.
procedure: Construct a raw barometer sample record with known pressure and temperature values.
Call the mlog write API for barometer records with the constructed sample.
Flush the run and re-open the produced log file.
Parse records and locate the barometer record.
Compare every barometer field against the input sample.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Write API returns success and the parsed barometer record exactly matches the input pressure and temperature values, with the record type identifying it as a barometer record.

test_cases.title: Raw GPS NMEA Sentence Verbatim Preservation
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog library against a tmpfs/in-memory storage backend with a fresh run.
procedure: Prepare a known NMEA sentence byte buffer including the leading '$' and trailing CRLF.
Call the mlog write API for NMEA records with the buffer and its length.
Flush the run and re-open the produced log file.
Parse records and extract the NMEA payload bytes from the located NMEA record.
Byte-compare the extracted payload against the original input buffer.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The bytes preserved in the NMEA record are byte-identical to the input sentence, with no truncation, escaping, reordering, or modification.

test_cases.title: Navigation State Record Write - Round Trip
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog library against a tmpfs/in-memory storage backend with a fresh run.
procedure: Construct a navigation state record with known position, velocity, and attitude fields.
Call the mlog write API for navigation records with the constructed state.
Flush the run and re-open the produced log file.
Parse records and locate the navigation record.
Compare every navigation field against the input state.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Write API returns success and the parsed navigation record exactly matches the input position, velocity, and attitude, with the record type identifying it as navigation state.

test_cases.title: AFM Phase Event Record Write - Round Trip
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog library against a tmpfs/in-memory storage backend with a fresh run.
procedure: Construct an AFM flight phase event record describing a known phase transition (e.g., PRE_LAUNCH to BOOST).
Call the mlog write API for AFM phase event records with the constructed event.
Flush the run and re-open the produced log file.
Parse records and locate the AFM event record.
Compare the recorded phase transition fields against the input event.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Write API returns success and the parsed AFM event record exactly matches the input phase transition, with the record type identifying it as an AFM event.

test_cases.title: GPS UTC Time Record Write - Round Trip
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog library against a tmpfs/in-memory storage backend with a fresh run.
procedure: Construct a GPS UTC time record with known UTC time-of-day and date fields plus a monotonic timestamp.
Call the mlog write API for GPS UTC records with the constructed record.
Flush the run and re-open the produced log file.
Parse records and locate the GPS UTC record.
Compare every UTC and timestamp field against the input record.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Write API returns success and the parsed GPS UTC record exactly matches the input UTC fields and the monotonic timestamp, with the record type identifying it as GPS UTC.

test_cases.title: Per-Record Monotonic Microsecond Timestamp Stamping
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog library with an injectable monotonic time source returning configurable microsecond values.
procedure: Set the time source to return a sequence of strictly increasing microsecond values.
Write one record of each type (IMU, barometer, NMEA, navigation, AFM event, GPS UTC) interleaved with time advances.
Flush the run and re-open the produced log file.
Parse all records and extract the embedded timestamp from each.
Compare each record's embedded timestamp against the time source value at the moment of its write call.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every parsed record carries the exact microsecond timestamp returned by the time source at its write call, and timestamps are strictly non-decreasing across the run.

test_cases.title: New Run Created on Each Initialization
test_cases.setup: Point mlog at an empty storage directory.
procedure: Initialize mlog, write at least one record, and tear down the library.
Initialize mlog a second time against the same storage directory and tear down.
Initialize mlog a third time against the same storage directory and tear down.
Enumerate the run artifacts present in the storage directory.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Three distinct, separately identifiable run artifacts exist in the storage directory after the three initializations, none aliasing one another.

test_cases.title: Prior Run Preservation Across Reinitialization
test_cases.setup: Point mlog at an empty storage directory.
procedure: Initialize mlog, write a known sequence of records ('Run A'), then tear down.
Capture the byte contents of the Run A artifact(s).
Initialize mlog a second time against the same directory, write a different sequence ('Run B'), then tear down.
Re-read the Run A artifact(s) from disk and compare bytes against the captured copy.
Confirm Run B artifact(s) exist and do not overlap or alias Run A storage.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Run A artifacts are byte-identical before and after Run B is created, and Run B did not delete or modify any Run A artifact.

test_cases.title: Machine-Parseable Format with Record Type Identifier
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog and prepare one record of every supported type.
procedure: Write one IMU, one barometer, one NMEA, one navigation, one AFM event, and one GPS UTC record in a known order.
Flush the run and re-open the produced log file.
Run the documented parser over the bytes from start to end without prior knowledge of record order.
For each parsed record, read the record type identifier and dispatch to the matching decoder.
Verify all six expected record types are recovered and decoded successfully.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The parser recovers exactly six records in the order written, each with a correctly identified record type, and decodes every payload without parse errors.

test_cases.title: Write Failure Status Returned to Caller
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog with a mock storage backend whose write call can be configured to return failure on demand.
procedure: Configure the mock backend to succeed for the first write call.
Write one IMU record and verify success status is returned.
Configure the mock backend to fail on the next write call.
Write another IMU record and capture the returned status.
Inspect the returned status code.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The mlog write API returns a non-success failure status when the underlying backend write fails, distinguishable from the success status returned for the prior call.

test_cases.title: Continue Accepting Writes After Failure
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog with a mock storage backend whose write call can be configured to fail or succeed per call.
procedure: Write one record (Record 1) with the backend in success mode and verify success.
Configure the backend to fail on the next write and write Record 2; verify failure status.
Reconfigure the backend to succeed on subsequent writes.
Write Record 3 and Record 4 and verify each returns success status.
Flush, re-open the run, and parse to enumerate persisted records.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The mlog library returns success for Record 1, Record 3, and Record 4 after the Record 2 failure, and Records 1, 3, and 4 are persisted in the run; the library does not refuse subsequent writes after a failure.

test_cases.title: POSIX and Pico2 Functional Equivalence
test_cases.setup: Build mlog for both POSIX (host) and Pico2 (RP2350) targets. Prepare a fixed scripted record sequence covering all record types with deterministic timestamps.
procedure: Run the scripted sequence on the POSIX build and capture the produced log file bytes.
Run the same scripted sequence on the Pico2 build and capture the produced log file bytes.
Compute a byte-level diff between the two captured outputs.
Parse both outputs with the documented parser and compare the recovered record sequences field-by-field.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Both builds accept every scripted call with the same status codes, and the parsed record sequences are field-by-field identical between POSIX and Pico2 outputs.

test_cases.title: Deterministic Byte Output for Identical Input
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog with a deterministic monotonic time source and a tmpfs storage backend.
procedure: Run a fixed scripted sequence of writes covering all record types and capture the produced byte stream as Output A.
Tear down mlog and reset the storage directory and time source to identical initial state.
Run the exact same scripted sequence and capture the produced byte stream as Output B.
Compute SHA-256 hashes of Output A and Output B.
Perform a byte-level comparison of Output A against Output B.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Output A and Output B are byte-identical and their SHA-256 hashes match exactly.

test_cases.title: Mixed Record Type Stream Round Trip
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog with a deterministic monotonic time source and a tmpfs storage backend.
procedure: Build a randomized-but-seeded sequence of 1000 records spanning all six record types with unique payloads per record.
Write the entire sequence and flush the run.
Re-open the produced log file and parse all records using the documented format.
Verify the parsed record count equals 1000 and every payload field matches the corresponding input record.
Verify every parsed record carries a monotonic microsecond timestamp consistent with the time source at the time of its write.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All 1000 records are recovered with correct record types, payloads matching the input by field, and monotonically non-decreasing timestamps consistent with the time source.

test_cases.title: Run Identity Distinguishes Sequential Runs
test_cases.setup: Point mlog at an empty storage directory.
procedure: Initialize mlog and write a tagged 'A' record, then tear down.
Initialize mlog again and write a tagged 'B' record, then tear down.
Enumerate run artifacts and parse each.
Verify exactly one run contains the 'A' record and a distinct run contains the 'B' record.
Verify neither run contains records from the other.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Two distinct runs exist, each containing only its own tagged record, with no cross-contamination of records between runs.

test_cases.title: Write Failure Does Not Corrupt Subsequent Records
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog with a mock storage backend supporting per-call success/failure injection.
procedure: Write IMU Record 1 in success mode.
Inject failure and write IMU Record 2; capture the returned failure status.
Restore success mode and write IMU Records 3, 4, and 5 with distinct known payloads.
Flush, re-open the run, and parse all records.
Verify each successfully-written record decodes cleanly with payload matching its input.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Records 1, 3, 4, and 5 are all recovered with correct payloads and identifiable record types; the failed Record 2 does not produce a malformed record that breaks parsing of subsequent records.
